## Stack

| PR | What |
| --- | --- |
| [#8031](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/pull/8031) | Keep what changes while a request is in flight |
| 👉 **this** | `ssr: false` for queries only a browser can run |

## Why

- A query the server can't run (the browser's session, `localStorage` in its input) had no way to stay off the server. `.query()` in a server render started it anyway.

## What

```ts
const post = trpc.post.byId.query({ id }, { ssr: false });
```

- On a server store, without data, it starts nothing. Its promise rejects with an error whose `digest` is `BAILOUT_TO_CLIENT_SIDE_RENDERING` (the one Next.js gives `next/dynamic` with `ssr: false`), so `use()` renders the Suspense fallback and the browser renders the boundary.
- It's the entry's own promise, so `useQuery` reads it; a later read without `ssr: false` starts the request.
- On a browser store it changes nothing. New types: `ReadOptions`, `ReactQueryArgs`.

## Links

- [`experimental-react.md` › Server rendering](https://github.com/trpc/trpc/blob/feat/react-ssr-false/www/v12/docs/integrations/experimental-react.md): new paragraph and example. Preview URLs not generated here.

## Alternatives considered

- A `skipToken`-style sentinel (TanStack): it disables the query everywhere, but the browser should still run it.

## Testing

- `dom.test.tsx`: "ssr: false: the server renders the fallback and sends nothing…" fails without it (the server render requests the post).
